column3: NKJV has “more signs than these,” following the Textus Receptus wording; the critical text reads “Will He do more signs than this man has done?”
NKJV has “the Pharisees and the chief priests,” reversing the Greek order “the chief priests and the Pharisees.”
Close to the Greek; “belly” is rendered “heart.”
NKJV has “the Holy Spirit,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “the Spirit.” NKJV supplies “given.”
NKJV has “many from the crowd” and “this saying,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “some of the crowd, having heard these words.”
NKJV includes “like this Man,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “No man ever spoke like this.”
NKJV has “came to Jesus by night,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “who came to Him before.”
NKJV has “no prophet has arisen,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the present “no prophet arises.”
NKJV includes 7:53–8:11 as normal text; the critical text prints this passage but marks it as a later addition.
